definitions.frontier: A named, versioned and owner-declared set of evidence objects with an explicit commitment and provenance boundary.
definitions.query: A canonical, versioned predicate bound to request, operation, purpose, recipient, jurisdiction and project snapshot.
definitions.included: An in-scope frontier item represented in the exact package's transitive source lineage.
definitions.withheld: An in-scope item not disclosed because a separately qualified restriction applies.
definitions.unavailable: An in-scope item whose content or authoritative resolver cannot currently be obtained.
definitions.excluded: An item explicitly outside the exact query scope.
definitions.unresolved: An item whose scope or disposition cannot be safely established.
definitions.complete: All items in the exact committed frontier have exactly one disposition and the included set is bound to the package; it is not global real-world completeness.

invariants.statement: The evidence frontier is explicitly named, versioned, committed and source-owner attributed.
The query commitment binds the exact request, operation, purpose, recipient, jurisdiction and project snapshot.
Each frontier object reference occurs exactly once in the private partition.
The partition's object-reference set equals the committed frontier's object-reference set.
Every in-scope item has exactly one of included, withheld, unavailable or unresolved.
Every out-of-scope item has the excluded disposition and cannot be silently included.
Unknown scope or disposition is unresolved; it is never converted to absent or excluded.
The included frontier set equals the terminal source-leaf set of the exact package's validated transitive transformation lineage.
No package output is introduced without a path to a source leaf in the committed frontier.
The query, request, recipient, package and frontier commitments are the exact same versions used in the proof.
Receipt freshness, signature, issuer trust and VDS proof validity are resolved by Mycelix's authoritative verifier.
Non-inclusion is bounded to the exact VDS and frontier version and is never presented as real-world absence.
The public verifier view does not expose protected object references, locations, claimant data, revealing counts or deterministic low-entropy hashes.
Proof visibility and detail are scoped to the verifier's operation-specific authority.
Every correction or new source event creates an explicit version/supersession; frozen frontier commitments are immutable.
Custody exit restores the frontier, query, partition semantics, receipt references and package relationships without the original provider's credentials.

partition_rule.set_equation: F_v = I disjoint_union W disjoint_union U disjoint_union X disjoint_union R
partition_rule.package_binding: I equals the package's transitive terminal source-leaf set

verifier_profiles.minimum_disclosure: exact package commitment and the object-level inclusion proof needed to verify items received
proof that the named query and partition were evaluated against the committed frontier, with only approved aggregate facts
opaque scoped receipt reference and consistency proof, if disclosure is authorized
full private partition and provenance required for its authorized stewardship role

non_goals: new CTER identity or authority system
automatic consent or community mandate resolution
claim that a receipt proves source acquisition was honest
public disclosure of withheld object inventory
